svg.title: Carrying passengers: three takeoffs and landings in 90 days, day and night
svg.desc: Two rules from 14 CFR 61.57 for a pilot in command carrying persons. Any time: three takeoffs and three landings in the preceding 90 days, as sole manipulator of the controls, in the same category, class and type if a type rating is required; for a tailwheel airplane the takeoffs and landings are to a full stop in a tailwheel airplane. Night, in addition, from 1 hour after sunset to 1 hour before sunrise: three takeoffs and three landings, each to a full stop, made in that night period within the preceding 90 days, as sole manipulator, in the same category, class and type if required.
svg.text: Recent experience to carry passengers (61.57)
For the pilot in command of an aircraft carrying persons. The 90 days count back from the day of the flight.
The last 90 days
3 takeoffs and 3 landings, you on the controls
90 days before
day of the flight
Any time: carrying persons
3 takeoffs and 3 landings in the preceding 90 days
You were the sole manipulator of the flight controls
Same category and class, and type if a class or type rating is required
Tailwheel airplane: takeoffs and landings to a full stop, in a tailwheel airplane
Night: carrying persons (also)
Night here means 1 hour after sunset to 1 hour before sunrise
night rule period
outside it
outside it
1 hour after sunset
1 hour before sunrise
3 takeoffs and 3 landings, each to a full stop, made in that period within 90 days
Sole manipulator; same category and class, and type if a type rating is required
Landings outside that period do not count for the night rule.
To build up these takeoffs and landings you may act as PIC under day VFR or day IFR with no
persons or property aboard other than those needed for the flight (61.57(a)(2)).
Source: 14 CFR 61.57(a), (b)
